AI
experiences are intent-driven and are beginning to work at task scope. We are entering an age of
macro-delegation and micro-steering across domains. Intelligence using multiple models is built
into multiple form factors. You see this in chat, in new agent inbox apps, coworker scaffoldings,
agent workflows embedded in applications and IDEs that are used every day, or even in our
command line with file system access and skills. That's the approach we are taking with our first-
party family of Copilot spanning key domains.
In consumer, for example, Copilot experiences span chat, news, feed, search, creation, browsing,
shopping, and integrations into the operating system, and it's gaining momentum. Daily users of
our Copilot app increase nearly 3x year-over-year, and with Copilot Checkout, we are partnered
with PayPal, Shopify, and Stripe, so customers can make purchases directly within the app. With
Microsoft 365 Copilot, we are focused on organization-wide productivity. Work IQ takes the data
underneath Microsoft 365 and creates the most valuable, stateful agent for every organization.
It delivers powerful reasoning capabilities over people, their roles, their artifacts, their
communications, and their history and memory, all within an organization's security boundary.
Microsoft 365 Copilot's accuracy and latency powered by Work IQ is unmatched, delivering faster
and more accurate work-grounded results than competition. And we have seen our biggest
quarter-over-quarter improvement in response quality to date. This has driven record usage

Copilot also is becoming true daily habit with daily active users increasing 10x year-over-year.

a trio of M365 advancements:
1. Agent 365 announced at $15 per user per month, a control plane for managing 
agents. New SKU will be generally available on May 1, 2026.
2. New E7 SKU announced at $99 per user per month, incl M365 E5, Entra Suite, 
Agent 365, and M365 Copilot. New SKU will be generally available on May 1, 2026.

both see accelerated adoption via E7 SKU. Note: recent M365 price hikes already force 
enterprise negotiations in 2H26, creating NT adoption catalyst.

We continue 
to see more evidence of steadily growing traction, including new disclosure this 
quarter of 15m paid M365 Copilot seats (accelerating q/q and +160% y/y), paid 
GitHub Copilot subs now up to 4.7m (+75% y/y) and >100k medical providers using 
Dragon Copilot, but likely not yet tangible enough in financial results for investors 
to feel like they are seeing high impact from an ROIC perspective.
Bringing it back to a high level perspective, we think some of the debate and nuance 
around near-term bogeys, while important, is missing a story of exceptional share 
gains and execution. Amidst a heavy investment cycle and supply constraints, the 
company is poised to deliver a third straight year of mid-teens+ growth in operating 
income (incl. y/y margin expansion) and non-GAAP EPS. With continued strong 
demand signal from backlog (Commercial RPO +28% y/y ex-OAI) we remain 
confident in the durability of top- and bottom-line trajectories over the next several 
years. We maintain our Buy rating while adjusting our target price to $575 (from 
$630) to reflect our updated estimates and thoughts on the business and market.

By segment, Intelligent Cloud (incl. Azure) and PBP exceeded expectations,
although MPC was surprisingly only roughly in line. Much more detail below.
Good Azure Performance, But with Allocations Constraining Growth Somewhat
Azure revenue growth of 38% Y/Y CC exceeded mgmt's guidance that had called for
37% growth, although this did fall shy of buy-side expectations (and slightly below the
39% growth in F1Q). On the heels of a strong first quarter, F2Q Commercial bookings
astoundingly grew 228% Y/Y CC, with the vast majority of the growth driven by Azure
commitments from both OpenAI and Anthropic. Mgmt did also note that having to
allocate additional capacity to certain first-party applications (such as M365 Copilot), as
well as to R&D, weighed on Azure growth this quarter by at least a couple of points.
Encouraging Azure Growth Outlook, with F3Q Revenue in Line
MSFT provided F3Q revenue guidance of $80.6B-$81.75B (15%-17% Y/Y) that was in line
with the Street's $81.2B target. More importantly, mgmt is targeting Azure revenue growth
of 37-38% Y/Y CC, slightly above the Street's roughly 36-37% Y/Y projection. Meanwhile,
mgmt stated that it expects capex to be down Q/Q. More on guidance below.
Valuation
Using an AH price of $452 (-6%), MSFT trades at a CY26E-27E P/E multiple of 26x and
21x-22x, and a temporarily elevated CY27E EV/FCF multiple of ~31x during this higher
capital intensity period. Our $620 PT (unchanged) is largely based on our updated sum-of-
the-parts model. Our price target also reflects a CY26E-27E P/E multiple of ~35x and 29x.

Office Range
As part of several product announcements, MSFT today
introduced an E7 SKU to its Office line-up. E7 will combine the
E5 capabilities with Copilot and Agent 365, and represents a
clear up-sell opportunity. We like this move as it harmonizes
the fragmenting Office plus Add-On landscape. 
The Office Suite is one of MSFT's largest franchises, with over 400mn users. Seat growth has
been one growth factor but upside here is limited (mostly entry level expansions), and hence
capturing greater value has been the more important driver of growth. In this respect, we like
the introduction of E7 today as it enables the continuation of MSFT's upsell strategy by bundling
more value into an offering at a higher price point. E7 should increase investors' confidence that
MSFT can maintain solid Office growth (currently around mid-teens level YoY) for longer. We also
note the launch of Wave 3 for MSFT Copilot which includes the offering of Anthropic's models
(beside OpenAI) and Claude Cowork capabilities and cements MSFT's role as a successful fast
follower of new technology.
When MSFT launched Copilot a while ago, many investors asked why it was not part of a new
SKU (E7 for example). At the time, it seemed MSFT wanted to make Copilot available to a
broader audience (not just the high-end SKU customers) and hence the separate pricing.

We are in the
beginning phases of AI diffusion and its broad GDP impact. Our TAM will grow substantially across

When it comes to our cloud and token factory, the key to long-term competitiveness is shaping
our infrastructure to support new high-scale workloads. We're building this infrastructure out for
the heterogeneous and distributed nature of these workloads, ensuring the right fit with the
geographic and segment-specific needs for all customers, including the long tail. The key metric
we're optimizing for is tokens per watt per dollar, which comes down to increasing utilization and
decreasing TCO using silicon, systems, and software.
A good example of this is the 50% increase in throughput we were able to achieve in one of our
highest volume workloads, OpenAI inferencing, powering our Copilots. And another example was

and thereby improve both performance and latencies for high-scale training.
